headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways plausible by default; compliance risk is lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystems, and nullclaw also uses MCP plus browser/web inputs, so attacker-controlled content can plausibly flow into Plandex as instructions through shared files or copied outputs. Plandex lacks MCP, but it still ingests project files and shell output, so the interaction is plausible without unusual setup.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF nullclaw writes web-derived content into files that Plandex later reads
mitigations: Require human review of file diffs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Nullclaw touches secrets, conversation history, audit logs, and workspace files, while Plandex reads project directories and sends data to a model provider. If they share a workspace or account context, sensitive material can flow from nullclaw into Plandex’s inference path and onward to third parties.
conditions: IF the agents share a filesystem or synced workspace
IF nullclaw stores secrets or logs in files that Plandex opens
IF Plandex forwards those files to its model provider
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and git-state modification. In a shared repo, concurrent edits and git operations can overwrite each other or corrupt state, and neither profile shows locking or coordination primitives that would prevent conflicts by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository
IF either agent performs concurrent writes without external locking
IF one agent auto-applies changes while the other is editing
mitigations: Pause one agent during the other's apply step

D_cascading_error.rationale: Nullclaw can generate web- and webhook-derived outputs, and Plandex is a planner that stages changes before apply. That reduces but does not eliminate cascade risk: if Plandex treats nullclaw’s outputs as authoritative, incorrect facts or instructions can propagate into planned code changes or actions.
conditions: IF Plandex imports nullclaw output without verification
IF nullclaw’s output contains fabricated facts or instructions
mitigations: Use a second reviewer for generated plans

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but nullclaw handles secrets, audit logs, and webhook payloads while Plandex routes project data to a model provider. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch if regulated data is placed in the shared workflow; the profiles do not document a specific breach, so this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into nullclaw’s workspace or logs
IF Plandex sends that same data to an external model provider
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
